_: The palette, the spacing and the type, once.
Both apps used to keep their own copy: :root in styles.css and T in
theme.ts, written by hand and drifting apart a value at a time — the line
colour was 0.08 on the laptop and 0.09 on the phone, there were three
greens and three ambers between them, and twelve different white overlays
This is the source. scripts/tokens.py writes both files from it, so a
colour changed here changes on both screens or on neither.
The surfaces are a ladder: bg is the floor, and everything that sits on
something else takes the next rung up. A card on a sheet, a field on a
card. Nothing skips a rung, and nothing invents a colour between two.

bg.note: The floor: the sidebar, the rail, the app behind everything.

bg-main.note: The conversation, a shade off the floor so the sidebar has an edge.

panel.note: Lifted over the app with nothing dimmed behind it: the tour's card, and a sheet on the phone. Dialogs on the desktop sit on the app's own ground instead.

field.note: Something you type in or choose from, on the app's own ground.

raised.note: The top rung: what has to read as in front of a field.

fill-1.note: A group of rows on a sheet.

fill-2.note: A control at rest: a chip, a tab.

hover.note: Under the pointer, and only there.

active.note: The row you are in, in a list.

branch.note: The line threads hang from in the sidebar.

on-accent.note: Type on blue, red or green.

bright.note: A surface that stays light whatever sits behind it: the send button, a live pill.

on-bright.note: Ink on that surface. inkOn() picks between this and on-accent.

blue.note: The one accent: what is chosen, what is yours to press.

link.note: Blue that has to stay legible in a paragraph.

amber.note: Wants you: a mention, a warning that is not a failure.

red.note: Gone wrong, or about to be destroyed.

space._: Fours, and a name for each so a gap can be argued about by name.

type._: Seven sizes. A screen that needs an eighth is a screen with a problem the type cannot fix.

row._: One height for a settings row on either screen, so a column of them has a rhythm.

font.sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "Segoe UI", Inter, sans-serif

layout._: Numbers the layout is built on, rather than colours or gaps.

sidebar-w.note: The rail of bots down the left.

chat-min.note: The narrowest a conversation may be shown at. MIN_CHAT_WIDTH in main.ts is the same number, so the script and the grid agree about when a pane has to go.

swatches._: What a bot can be. Deliberately not a scale — these are people, not levels.
